summary: Tark Hill tower near Suscon and Dupont: built 1951, dismantled for an FAA site in 1960. A storymap's Bear Springs tower (dated 1959) may be a different structure. Site today unknown.

facts.status_note: The register lists it as a former site. The storymap's Bear Springs tower was replaced in 2018; it does not say a structure stands at this site.

staffing.status: operated by James J. Reap; last recorded operator 1955

events.note: Register gives 1951 and the 1951 notice says the tower was located there to replace Big Shinny Tower
Opened with James Reap in charge
Notice lists James Reap as operator
Storymap date for the tower it calls Bear Springs; no other source gives it and none ties that tower to this site
Tark Hill tower dismantled because the FAA wanted the site for a VORTAC facility
Register gives 1960 as the replacement year; the August 1960 notice describes a new 90-foot tower south of Dupont
Storymap says the Bear Springs tower was replaced in 2018; no source ties that tower to this site

corrections.why: The 1955 notice lists Tark Hill among the Luzerne County towers, but the transcription heading for the 1951 notice says Lackawanna County, so a human should check it.

corrections.proposed: 1951 (register and 1951 notice), with the storymap's 1959 kept as a disputed date
corrections.why: The register and the 1951 and 1952 notices date the Tark Hill tower to 1951; the 1959 date comes only from the storymap.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register lists the site as former. The storymap says the tower was replaced in 2018 and does not say a structure stands here, so the record's note that the storymap says standing is not supported by the text read.
The storymap gives 80 feet for Bear Springs and the August 1960 notice gives 90 feet for the new tower south of Dupont. Neither is confirmed as the Tark Hill tower's height, so no height is recorded.
Register and 1951 notices give 1951; the storymap gives 1959 for the Bear Springs tower. No source links the two dates.

notes_for_editor: Four sources, none describing the site today. The storymap web page is script-only, so its text is cited through the ArcGIS item data URL that was read. The record joins the Tark Hill and Bear Springs names on nearly identical coordinates (storymap 41.2628, -75.7062; record 41.2629, -75.7061), but no source says the 1960 replacement is the storymap's Bear Springs tower. Newspaper quotes come from the transcriptions on the Eastern US Lookouts page, not from the original papers. No height or access is recorded for the Tark Hill tower: the storymap's 80 feet, Aermotor maker and State Game Lands 91 location apply to Bear Springs, which no source ties to this site.
